lead: A chain drive pulls a roller chain over two sprockets. The rollers sit in the tooth gaps, so the chain cannot slip and the velocity ratio is fixed by the tooth counts. It carries more torque than a belt in the same space, works hot and in oil, and runs motorcycles, conveyors and camshafts. Its costs are chordal action, which makes the speed pulse, and the sliding pin-bush hinge, which needs oil and slowly wears the chain longer.
prereq: You need: the place of a chain among flexible drives from flexible drives and belt materials, and the service-factor habit from design of V-belt drives.

blocks.text: A roller chain is a set of short links. Pins are pressed into the outer plates; bushes are pressed into the inner plates and turn on the pins; rollers turn freely on the bushes. As the chain bends onto a sprocket, the pin turns inside its bush: this hinge is where sliding, and so wear, happens. The roller rolls onto the tooth, so the tooth sees little rubbing.

Types: roller chain (bush roller chain) for power transmission; silent or inverted-tooth chain, where shaped plates engage the sprocket teeth and there are no rollers, used at high speed and low noise; block chain, simple cast blocks for low speed; detachable chain, hooked links for farm machinery.

The standard number fixes the pitch p (distance between pin centres), the roller diameter and the inner width. ISO 08B has p = 12.7 mm and ISO 10B has p = 15.875 mm; a suffix gives the strands, so 08B-1 is single and 08B-2 duplex. ANSI 40 and ANSI 50 are the US-series chains with the same two pitches. Give the full number when ordering: two chains with the same pitch can have different rollers and will not fit the same sprocket.

Let Z₁ be the teeth on the small sprocket, Z₂ on the large, p the pitch and N₁ the small-sprocket speed in rev/min. The mean chain speed is exactly v = Z₁pN₁/60, one pitch per tooth passed. πd₁N₁/60 is the speed of a point on the pitch circle, the largest link speed; the two differ by less than 1 % for Z ≥ 17. The worked example uses the mean speed for the chain pull.

blocks.where: v is the mean chain speed in m/s; Z₁ is the teeth on the small sprocket; p is the pitch in m; N₁ is its speed in rev/min.

blocks.text: The pitch diameter is the circle through the roller centres, not the tip circle. A 19-tooth 08B sprocket has d = 12.7/sin 9.474° = 77.16 mm.

blocks.where: d is the pitch diameter; p is the pitch; Z is the number of teeth. Work the angle 180°/Z in degrees.

blocks.text: Chordal action: the chain wraps the sprocket as a polygon, so the link speed rises and falls between πdN/60 and πdN/60 × cos(180°/Z). The fractional fall is 1 − cos(180°/Z): 4.0 % at Z = 11 and 1.36 % at Z = 19. Few teeth also mean a smaller pitch diameter, so the same torque gives a higher chain pull. Use at least 17 teeth, and 19 or more for smooth running.
Chain length is counted in pitches (links). Round it up to an even number, because an odd count needs an offset link; then find the exact centre distance for that count.

blocks.where: L is the chain length in pitches; C is the centre distance; p is the pitch. For a chosen even L, the exact centre distance is C = (p/4)[A + √(A² − 8B²)], with A = L − (Z₁ + Z₂)/2 and B = (Z₂ − Z₁)/(2π).

blocks.text: Failure modes: fatigue of the link plates under the fluctuating tension; impact fatigue of rollers and bushes at each engagement with the sprocket; wear of pins and bushes, which lengthens the pitch and the chain; roller wear, which damages the tooth seating; galling of pin and bush when the oil film breaks down at high speed and load; and the chain riding up and jumping teeth once it has stretched. Makers usually set the replacement limit between about 1.5 % and 3 % elongation, the smaller figure for large sprockets.

items: Service factor K<sub>s</sub> from the driver, the driven machine and the hours per day; design power = K<sub>s</sub> × motor power.
Z₁ ≥ 17 (19 for smooth running) and Z₂ = iZ₁, where i is the speed ratio.
From the maker’s chart, the first chain whose rating at N₁ is at least the design power.
C of about 30p to 50p; L rounded up to even links; the exact C for those links.
Factor of safety on breaking load, lubrication method and shaft loads.

blocks.text: Lubrication: brush or manual oiling for low speed; drip feed; bath or disc lubrication for enclosed drives; spray for high speed. Oil must reach the pin-bush hinge. Grease is for sealed motorcycle chains, not for high-speed industrial chains. Leave a small slack-side sag, roughly 2% of centre distance; too tight a chain overloads shafts and bearings. Use an idler or move the motor to adjust.

figure.caption: The chain drive of the worked example, drawn to scale, and the link speed as the small sprocket turns. The speed dips by 1.36 % once per tooth because the chain leaves the 19-tooth sprocket as a polygon.

spec.aria: Two sprockets with 19 and 38 teeth on a 503.4 millimetre centre distance with the tight and sagging slack strands; below, a wave of link speed between 4.040 and 3.985 metres per second around the 4.022 mean.

examples.question: A 3 kW, 1000 rpm electric motor drives a compressor at 500 rpm through a single-strand 08B roller chain (p = 12.7 mm, breaking load 17.8 kN). Z₁ = 19, Z₂ = 38 and the centre distance is about 500 mm. The service factor is 1.3, and the maker’s chart rates one strand of 08B at 4.5 kW at 1000 rpm on a 19-tooth sprocket. Check the chain, and find the pitch diameters, the chain speed, the chain pull, the factor of safety, the number of links with the exact centre distance, and the speed variation. Neglect centrifugal tension and sag.
steps: Speed ratio: Z₂/Z₁ = 38/19 = 2, so the compressor turns at 1000/2 = 500 rpm.
Design power: 1.3 × 3 = 3.9 kW. The 08B rating of 4.5 kW is above it, so a single strand of 08B is acceptable.
Mean chain speed: v = Z₁pN₁/60 = 19 × 0.0127 × 1000/60 = 4.022 m/s.
Factor of safety on breaking load: 17 800/746 = 23.9. The chain is far from breaking; the power rating, which allows for plate fatigue and wear, is the real limit.
Speed variation: 1 − cos 9.474° = 1 − 0.98636 = 0.0136, or 1.36 %. The link speed swings between π × 0.07716 × 1000/60 = 4.040 m/s and 4.040 × 0.98636 = 3.985 m/s.
examples.answer: One strand of 08B is enough (3.9 kW design power against a 4.5 kW rating). d₁ = 77.16 mm, d₂ = 153.79 mm, v = 4.02 m/s, F = 746 N, factor of safety 23.9, 108 links at a centre distance of 503.4 mm, and a speed variation of 1.36 %.
examples.check:
import math
p, Z1, Z2, C, N1, P, Q = 12.7, 19, 38, 500.0, 1000.0, 3000.0, 17800.0
d1 = p/math.sin(math.pi/Z1); d2 = p/math.sin(math.pi/Z2)
v = Z1*p*N1/60000; F = P/v
B = (Z2 - Z1)/(2*math.pi)
L = 2*C/p + (Z1 + Z2)/2 + B**2*p/C
n = math.ceil(L/2)*2; A = n - (Z1 + Z2)/2
Cx = p/4*(A + math.sqrt(A*A - 8*B*B))
print(round(d1, 2), round(d2, 2), round(v, 3), round(F), round(Q/F, 1), round(L, 2), n, round(Cx, 1), round(100*(1 - math.cos(math.pi/Z1)), 2))

traps: Rounding to an odd number of links. An odd count needs a weaker offset link; round up to even and recompute C: 108 links put the sprockets 503.4 mm apart, not 500 mm.
Using the tip diameter instead of the pitch diameter d = p/sin(180°/Z). The chain sits on the pitch circle.
Choosing a chain from the motor power alone. Compare the rating with the design power: 3.9 kW, not 3 kW, in the worked example.
Writing the speed variation as cos(180°/Z) instead of 1 − cos(180°/Z): 1.36 %, not 98.6 %, at 19 teeth.
Setting a chain as tight as a V-belt. It needs a little slack; too tight overloads the shaft bearings.

quiz.q: Name the parts of a roller chain link and say which one touches the sprocket tooth.
quiz.a: Pin, bush, roller, inner plate, outer plate; the roller touches the tooth.

quiz.q: Why is the velocity ratio of a chain drive exact, while a belt drive can slip?
quiz.a: The rollers sit in the tooth gaps, so the chain is pulled by positive contact and cannot slip. A belt depends on friction and can slip when overloaded.

quiz.q: An 08B chain (p = 12.7 mm) runs on a 17-tooth sprocket at 800 rpm. Find pitch diameter and average chain speed.
Why specify at least 19 teeth on the small sprocket for a smooth high-speed drive?
quiz.a: The speed variation is 1 − cos(180°/Z): 1.36 % at 19 teeth against 4.0 % at 11. More teeth reduce pulsation, noise and impact at engagement, and give a larger pitch diameter, which lowers the chain pull for the same torque.

quiz.q: A drive has design power 11 kW at 720 rpm. A 10B chain is rated 12 kW at 720 rpm. Is the chain acceptable?
quiz.a: Yes. The 12 kW rating is greater than the 11 kW design power, and the service factor is already inside the design power.

quiz.q: Why is an offset link avoided in a roller chain?
quiz.a: It is used to close an odd number of links. The offset link uses a cranked plate, so the pull is eccentric and the plate carries bending on top of tension; it is the weakest link and a common failure point.

quiz.q: A chain has elongated 2% and jumps teeth. Give the cause and the remedy.
quiz.a: Wear at pins and bushes increases pitch; the chain sits high on the teeth and skips. Replace chain and worn sprockets, restore correct sag and improve lubrication.

beyond: Not for the exam. Roller chains are chosen from makers’ catalogues that rate each chain by speed, tooth count and lubrication. High-speed engines use silent chains and toothed belts. Search "chain drive selection ISO 606" and "chain wear elongation".
